text:
Predicates:
Cost(greTest, 205) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test.
Cheaper(205, 300) ::: $205 is cheaper than $300.
ProvidesFinancialAid(ets, x) ::: ETS provides financial aid to x.
Applicant(x) ::: x is a GRE applicant.
ProvesEconomicHardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
LivesInSingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
HasFewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available to them.
LivesInSingleParentFamilyOrFewResources(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family or has few resources available to them.
TomLivesInSingleParentFamily ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
TomDadOutOfWork ::: Tom's dad has been out of work.
TomHasFewResources ::: Tom has few resources available to him.
ApplyingToTakeGRE(tom) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
TakingGRE(x) ::: x is taking the GRE test.
HasFinancialAid(x) ::: x has financial aid provided to them.

Premises:
Cost(greTest, 205) ∧ Cheaper(205, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
∀x ((Applicant(x) ∧ ProvesEconomicHardship(x)) → ProvidesFinancialAid(ets, x)) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x ((LivesInSingleParentFamily(x) ∨ HasFewResources(x)) → ProvesEconomicHardship(x)) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources available to them can prove economic hardship.
TomLivesInSingleParentFamily ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
TomDadOutOfWork ∧ TomHasFewResources ::: Tom's dad has been out of work, and Tom has few resources available to him.
ApplyingToTakeGRE(tom) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.

Conclusion:
¬∃x (TakingGRE(x) ∧ HasFinancialAid(x)) ::: No one taking the GRE test has financial aid provided to them by something.
